summary.title: Visual design rules you can safely follow every time
summary.one_liner: A set of opinionated visual design rules (contrast, neutrals, spacing scales, alignment, shadows, typography, grids) that the author considers safe to apply in nearly any interface.
takeaways: Avoid pure black and pure white; use close-to-black and close-to-white, and tint neutrals slightly toward your palette colour (under 5% HSB saturation).
Use a scale (e.g. multiples of 8) for spacing and sizing, measure gaps between high-contrast edges, and keep outer padding at least equal to inner padding.
Lighter elements appear closer to the user; keep shadows consistent throughout the interface and lower contrast on icons paired with text.
Nested rounded corners: inner radius = outer radius minus the gap; use 12-column grids for flexible layouts.
Keep body text at 16px or larger, keep line lengths around 60-80 characters, and limit typefaces to two.
summary.summary: The page is a short list of visual design rules written by Anthony Hobday, each framed as safe to follow by default but breakable with good reason. Each rule is explained in a few sentences and most are illustrated with before/after examples (images not included in the text). Topics range from colour (neutrals, contrast, brightness of borders and containers) to layout (alignment, scales, 12-column grids, visual weight ordering) and typography (text size, leading, line length, typeface count). It also covers depth and shadows, including how they behave in dark interfaces.
